_meta.indication: Treatment of non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis (NCFB) in adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older

pivotal_trials.design: 52-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter trial of BRINSUPRI 10 mg vs 25 mg vs placebo once daily
pivotal_trials.population: Adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older with non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis; adults had confirmed NCFB by chest CT with at least 2 pulmonary exacerbations in the prior 12 months
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Annualized rate of pulmonary exacerbations (PEx) over the 52-week treatment period
pivotal_trials.result: Annualized PEx rate 1.29 (placebo) vs 1.02 (10 mg) and 1.04 (25 mg); rate ratio 0.79 (95% CI 0.68, 0.92) for 10 mg and 0.81 (95% CI 0.69, 0.94) for 25 mg

pivotal_trials.phase: Phase 2 (supportive; phase 2 data supported breakthrough therapy designation)
pivotal_trials.design: 24-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in adults
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Time to first pulmonary exacerbation over the 24-week treatment period
pivotal_trials.result: Time to first PEx longer with BRINSUPRI; hazard ratio vs placebo 0.58 (10 mg) and 0.62 (25 mg); 95% CI 0.35 to 0.95 and 0.38 to 0.99

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=2% and more common than placebo): upper respiratory tract infection (25% placebo, 27% BRINSUPRI 10 mg, 29% BRINSUPRI 25 mg), headache, rash, dry skin, hyperkeratosis, hypertension. Only hyperkeratosis and gingivitis/periodontitis occurred at higher frequencies in the brensocatib groups compared to placebo.
target_moa: Brensocatib is a first-in-class reversible small molecule inhibitor of dipeptidyl peptidase 1 (DPP1, cathepsin C), which activates neutrophil serine proteases (NE, PR3, cathepsin G); inhibition reduces downstream NSP activity yielding broad anti-inflammatory effect

advisory_committee.vote: An advisory committee meeting was not required for this application

basis.text: Breakthrough therapy designation granted June 5, 2020 because there are no approved therapies for NCFB and phase 2 data showed clinically meaningful and statistically significant improvement in the primary endpoint

citations.quote: Since there are no approved therapies for NCFB and the phase 2 data demonstrated a clinically meaningful and statistically significant improvement in the primary endpoint, brensocatib received breakthrough therapy designation on June 5, 2020, and was reviewed on a priority timeline.

basis.text: The NDA was designated Priority review and reviewed on a priority timeline

citations.quote: Since there are no approved therapies for NCFB and the phase 2 data demonstrated a clinically meaningful and statistically significant improvement in the primary endpoint, brensocatib received breakthrough therapy designation on June 5, 2020, and was reviewed on a priority timeline.

summary.text: Brensocatib, a first-in-class DPP1 inhibitor, received breakthrough therapy designation on June 5, 2020 and was reviewed on a priority timeline; it received traditional (not accelerated) approval based on the phase 3 ASPEN trial, without an advisory committee meeting.

citations.quote: Since there are no approved therapies for NCFB and the phase 2 data demonstrated a clinically meaningful and statistically significant improvement in the primary endpoint, brensocatib received breakthrough therapy designation on June 5, 2020, and was reviewed on a priority timeline.

The Applicant, Insmed Incorporated, submitted an NDA for brensocatib, a first-in-class reversible inhibitor of dipeptidyl peptidase 1 (DPP1), for the treatment of non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis (NCFB) in patients aged 12 years and older.
An advisory committee meeting or other external consultations were not required as part of this application.

requirement.text: 4840-1 Conduct a 52-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel group study in children 6 to 11 years of age (inclusive) with non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis to assess efficacy, safety, and pharmacokinetic responses to brexucabib.
